title: editcap: Add --discard-name-resolution flag to strip embedded NRBs
description:
Adds a new --discard-name-resolution option to editcap that discards all
Name Resolution Block (NRB) entries from the input file when writing the
output file.

The option uses the existing wtap_dump_params_discard_name_resolution() API
in wiretap to filter out all hostname-to-IP mappings. This is useful for:
- Removing hostnames baked in at capture time before sharing files
- Stripping personal or internal naming schemes from captures
- Replacing embedded resolutions with local network mappings

The flag follows the same pattern as --discard-all-secrets and
--discard-capture-comment for consistency.

AI-Assisted: yes

notes.body:
> The option uses the existing wtap_dump_params_discard_name_resolution() API in wiretap to filter out all hostname-to-IP mappings.

It would filter out all hostname <-> any address mappings; if we were to support pcapng's hostname <-> MAC address mappings, it would filter those out, too.

I suspect that, from the point of view of most people using this option, that would be considered a feature rather than a bug. I.e., it strips out internal host name details that they might not want exposed.
added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 2
